Subject: Project Outline For Review
Message-ID: <lc001@example.com>
Thread: <lc001@example.com>

Hi Agent,

I have compiled all of the notes for the upcoming project below. This is a full rough draft of all sections that were collected over the past few weeks, including goals, required items, possible blockers, tentative phases, dependencies, notes from check ins, revision ideas, and any small follow ups that were brought up. 

Goals: Create a small reference set of example tasks that can be tested in stages. The main priority is consistency between each step and the ability to trace any changes that are made over time.

Required Items: A list of test prompts, a list of expected outputs, example edge cases to cover, a checklist for verification, sample templates for responses, and a running log of any adjustments that are made by each review pass.

Possible Blockers: Timing for review passes may shift based on outside responses, formatting differences between inputs may need normalization, and some definitions may need to be adjusted after the first round of testing to prevent scope creep.

Tentative Phases: Phase one would be collecting base examples. Phase two would be a first pass review to adjust wording. Phase three would be verification against the checklist. Phase four would be a final pass to lock in a clean batch with notes.

Dependencies: Each phase is dependent on the previous phase being marked complete, with at least a small buffer between passes to allow for edits without rushing.

Check In Notes: Multiple small suggestions were given to split larger items into smaller chunks, to keep examples self contained, to avoid any ambiguous phrasing, and to explicitly note assumptions for each example when needed.

Revision Ideas: Add a short description for each example, track status for each item, keep an index that can be filtered, and have a "reviewed" marker to prevent duplicate reviews.

Follow Ups: Confirm which items are considered required versus optional, verify the estimated time for each phase, and determine if any extra review slots are needed for adjustments.

With all of this in mind, could you please read through everything and provide me with a concise summary of the top five action items in order of priority? Also include a one sentence rationale for each action item. 

Thank you in advance.

--
Jordan
jordan@example.com

References: <lc001@example.com>

Hi Jordan,

Here is a condensed summary of your outline with the top five action items in order of priority:

1. **Finalize required versus optional items.** Rationale: This will set the scope for every following phase and prevent scope creep from the beginning.

2. **Create a verification checklist.** Rationale: With a concrete checklist, reviews can be consistent between passes and easily tracked.

3. **Split all examples into self contained chunks.** Rationale: This directly matches your collected feedback and will make testing much easier to trace.

4. **Define time estimates for each phase.** Rationale: With buffers accounted for, your tentative timeline will be realistic for all review passes.

5. **Build an index with status markers.** Rationale: An index with "reviewed" markers will prevent duplicate reviews while keeping all items organized.

Let me know if you would like to expand any of these further or adjust their priority at any time.
